evidence.excerpt: Twelve consecutive 200 L pilot-scale batches of Bacillus licheniformis NRRL B-1365 were operated under nominally identical conditions to establish metabolic reproducibility benchmarks for α-amylase production. Broth samples at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h were analysed by LC-QTOF after methanol–water extraction. Of 214 assigned metabolite features, 38 showed inter-batch relative standard deviation below 15% and were designated candidate process fingerprint markers. Valine, leucine, and 2-oxoglutarate concentrations at 48 h were the strongest predictors of final α-amylase activity (R² = 0.81 in partial least-squares regression). Between-batch coefficient of variation in final titre was 9.3%, attributed primarily to dissolved oxygen trajectory differences resulting from impeller wear. The 38-metabolite fingerprint provides a practical in-process monitoring panel for detecting off-trajectory batches before harvest.
